title: Dias round the Cape
span: 1487 to 1488, Lisbon to the Eastern Cape
summary: Bartolomeu Dias led the first European ships known to sail round the southern tip of Africa, opening a sea route to the Indian Ocean.
caveat: Dias's own report is lost; the voyage is known mainly from later Portuguese chronicles and from stone crosses he raised, one of which was found in pieces in 1938. Khoikhoi people had lived on these shores for centuries.

stops.title: Leaves Lisbon
stops.narration: Dias sailed with two caravels and a supply ship, ordered to find the end of Africa and a sea route east.
sources: Eric Axelson, Portuguese in South-East Africa, 1488-1600 (1973)
Joao de Barros, Decadas da Asia (1552)

stops.title: Angra Pequena
stops.narration: The fleet anchored in this bay on the desert coast. On the way home, Dias is said to have raised a stone cross on the nearby headland now called Dias Point.
stops.confidence_note: Chronicle dates differ; the cross site is shown approximately.
sources: Eric Axelson, Portuguese in South-East Africa, 1488-1600 (1973)

stops.title: Mossel Bay
stops.narration: After a storm blew the ships far south, Dias turned north and reached land here, past the Cape without seeing it. Khoikhoi herders drove the strangers off and one was killed by a Portuguese crossbow.
sources: Eric Axelson, Portuguese in South-East Africa, 1488-1600 (1973)
Joao de Barros, Decadas da Asia (1552)

stops.title: The cross at Kwaaihoek
stops.narration: Dias raised a stone cross, a padrao, on this headland. Its fragments were found and pieced together in 1938, and a replica stands here.
sources: Eric Axelson, Portuguese in South-East Africa, 1488-1600 (1973)

stops.title: Turning back
stops.place: Great Fish River mouth, Eastern Cape
stops.narration: With the coast clearly turning north-east toward India, the exhausted crew forced Dias to turn back near this river.
stops.confidence_note: The exact turning point is uncertain.
sources: Eric Axelson, Portuguese in South-East Africa, 1488-1600 (1973)
Joao de Barros, Decadas da Asia (1552)

stops.title: Cape of Good Hope
stops.place: Cape of Good Hope, Western Cape
stops.narration: On the way home Dias finally saw the cape. By tradition he named it the Cape of Storms, and King John II renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.
stops.confidence_note: The naming story comes from later chroniclers and may be legend.
sources: Joao de Barros, Decadas da Asia (1552)
